quests.question: Convert to reported speech: He said, 'I am ready.'
options: He said that he was ready.
He said that he is ready.
He said that I was ready.
quests.correctAnswer: He said that he was ready.
quests.sentence: He said, 'I am ready.'
quests.hint: Shift 'am' one step back in time to 'was'.
quests.explanation: In reported speech, present simple ('am') shifts to past simple ('was').

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She noted, 'I may come to the party.'
options: She noted that she might come to the party.
She noted that she may come to the party.
She noted that she would come to the party.
quests.correctAnswer: She noted that she might come to the party.
quests.sentence: She noted, 'I may come to the party.'
quests.hint: The modal 'may' becomes 'might' in reported speech.
quests.explanation: 'May' shifts to 'might' when backshifting modals in reported speech.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She advised, 'You should see a doctor.'
options: She advised me to see a doctor.
She advised that I see a doctor.
She said I should see a doctor.
quests.correctAnswer: She advised me to see a doctor.
quests.sentence: She advised, 'You should see a doctor.'
quests.hint: Advice is reported with 'advised + object + to + infinitive'.
quests.explanation: When reporting advice, use 'advised + object + to-infinitive'. 'You should see' becomes 'advised me to see'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She told me, 'We will arrive soon.'
options: She told me that they would arrive soon.
She told me that they will arrive soon.
She told me that we would arrive soon.
quests.correctAnswer: She told me that they would arrive soon.
quests.sentence: She told me, 'We will arrive soon.'
quests.hint: 'Will' shifts to 'would', and 'we' changes to 'they' (she is excluded from 'we').
quests.explanation: 'Will' becomes 'would' in reported speech. The pronoun 'we' shifts to 'they' because the speaker is reporting, not included.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The teacher said, 'Finish your homework.'
options: The teacher said that we finished our homework.
The teacher told us to finish our homework.
The teacher said finish our homework.
quests.correctAnswer: The teacher told us to finish our homework.
quests.sentence: The teacher said, 'Finish your homework.'
quests.hint: Imperatives (commands) are reported using 'told + object + to + infinitive'.
quests.explanation: Commands are reported with 'told + object + to + infinitive'. 'Finish your homework' becomes 'told us to finish our homework'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: He said, 'I must finish this report today.'
options: He said that he had to finish that report that day.
He said that he must finish this report today.
He said that he has to finish that report that day.
quests.correctAnswer: He said that he had to finish that report that day.
quests.sentence: He said, 'I must finish this report today.'
quests.hint: 'Must' shifts to 'had to', 'this' shifts to 'that', and 'today' shifts to 'that day'.
quests.explanation: 'Must' becomes 'had to', deictic 'this' becomes 'that', and the time reference 'today' shifts to 'that day'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The commander announced, 'I have finished the test.'
options: The commander announced that he had finished the test.
The commander announced that he finished the test.
The commander announced that he has finished the test.
quests.correctAnswer: The commander announced that he had finished the test.
quests.sentence: The commander announced, 'I have finished the test.'
quests.hint: Present perfect ('have finished') shifts to past perfect ('had finished').
quests.explanation: 'Have finished' (present perfect) shifts to 'had finished' (past perfect) in reported speech.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: He asked, 'Where are you going?'
options: He asked where was I going.
He asked where I am going.
He asked where I was going.
quests.correctAnswer: He asked where I was going.
quests.sentence: He asked, 'Where are you going?'
quests.hint: In reported questions, use statement word order: subject before verb.
quests.explanation: Reported questions use statement word order (subject + verb), not question order. 'Are you going' becomes 'I was going'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She said, 'I might come if I have time.'
options: She said that she might come if she had time.
She said that she might come if she has time.
She said that she might have come if she had time.
quests.correctAnswer: She said that she might come if she had time.
quests.sentence: She said, 'I might come if I have time.'
quests.hint: 'Might' stays as 'might'; the present 'have' in the conditional shifts to 'had'.
quests.explanation: 'Might' does not shift further. In the conditional clause, 'have' (present simple) shifts to 'had' (past simple).

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The pilot stated, 'The system is failing.'
options: The pilot stated that the system has failed.
The pilot stated that the system is failing.
The pilot stated that the system was failing.
quests.correctAnswer: The pilot stated that the system was failing.
quests.sentence: The pilot stated, 'The system is failing.'
quests.hint: Present continuous ('is failing') shifts to past continuous ('was failing').
quests.explanation: 'Is failing' (present continuous) becomes 'was failing' (past continuous) in reported speech.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She warned, 'Don't touch the wire.'
options: She warned me not to touch the wire.
She warned me don't touch the wire.
She warned me to not touch the wire.
quests.correctAnswer: She warned me not to touch the wire.
quests.sentence: She warned, 'Don't touch the wire.'
quests.hint: Negative imperatives are reported with 'warned + object + not to + infinitive'.
quests.explanation: Negative commands use 'warned/told + object + not to + infinitive'. 'Don't touch' becomes 'not to touch'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: They said, 'We ought to leave early.'
options: They said that they ought to leave early.
They said that they ought to have left early.
They said that they had to leave early.
quests.correctAnswer: They said that they ought to leave early.
quests.sentence: They said, 'We ought to leave early.'
quests.hint: 'Ought to' does not change in reported speech.
quests.explanation: 'Ought to' is one of the modal forms that remains unchanged in reported speech. It stays as 'ought to'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The doctor reported, 'I can help you.'
options: The doctor reported that he could help me.
The doctor reported that he can help me.
The doctor reported that I could help you.
quests.correctAnswer: The doctor reported that he could help me.
quests.sentence: The doctor reported, 'I can help you.'
quests.hint: 'Can' shifts to 'could' in reported speech. Pronouns also shift.
quests.explanation: 'Can' becomes 'could' in reported speech. 'I' changes to 'he' (the doctor) and 'you' changes to 'me'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: They said, 'We are staying here.'
options: They said that they were staying there.
They said that they were staying here.
They said that they are staying here.
quests.correctAnswer: They said that they were staying there.
quests.sentence: They said, 'We are staying here.'
quests.hint: 'Here' (deictic word) shifts to 'there' in reported speech. The tense also shifts.
quests.explanation: Both the tense ('are' → 'were') and the deictic word ('here' → 'there') shift in reported speech.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: He promised, 'I will call you tomorrow.'
options: He promised that he would call me the next day.
He promised that he will call me tomorrow.
He promised that he would call me tomorrow.
quests.correctAnswer: He promised that he would call me the next day.
quests.sentence: He promised, 'I will call you tomorrow.'
quests.hint: 'Will' shifts to 'would', 'you' to 'me', and 'tomorrow' to 'the next day'.
quests.explanation: Multiple changes occur: 'will' → 'would', 'you' → 'me', and the time word 'tomorrow' → 'the next day'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The scientist explained, 'We saw the signal.'
options: The scientist explained that they have seen the signal.
The scientist explained that they had seen the signal.
The scientist explained that they saw the signal.
quests.correctAnswer: The scientist explained that they had seen the signal.
quests.sentence: The scientist explained, 'We saw the signal.'
quests.hint: Past simple ('saw') shifts to past perfect ('had seen').
quests.explanation: 'Saw' (past simple) shifts to 'had seen' (past perfect) in reported speech.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: He asked her, 'Do you want some coffee?'
options: He asked her if she wanted some coffee.
He asked her if did she want some coffee.
He asked her whether she want some coffee.
quests.correctAnswer: He asked her if she wanted some coffee.
quests.sentence: He asked her, 'Do you want some coffee?'
quests.hint: Yes/No questions use 'if' or 'whether'. The auxiliary 'do' disappears and tense shifts.
quests.explanation: Yes/No questions are reported with 'if/whether'. The auxiliary 'do' is dropped, and 'want' shifts to 'wanted'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She told him, 'I saw her two days ago.'
options: She told him that she had seen her two days ago.
She told him that she had seen her two days before.
She told him that she saw her two days before.
quests.correctAnswer: She told him that she had seen her two days before.
quests.sentence: She told him, 'I saw her two days ago.'
quests.hint: 'Ago' shifts to 'before' in reported speech. Past simple also shifts to past perfect.
quests.explanation: 'Saw' shifts to 'had seen' (past perfect) and 'ago' shifts to 'before' - both standard reported speech changes.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: He said, 'I'm going to the store.'
options: He said that he was going to the store.
He said that he is going to the store.
He said that he goes to the store.
quests.correctAnswer: He said that he was going to the store.
quests.sentence: He said, 'I'm going to the store.'
quests.hint: Present continuous ('I'm going') shifts to past continuous ('was going').
quests.explanation: 'I'm going' (present continuous) becomes 'he was going' (past continuous). The pronoun 'I' shifts to 'he'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She asked, 'What time does the train leave?'
options: She asked what time the train left.
She asked what time did the train leave.
She asked what time the train leaves.
quests.correctAnswer: She asked what time the train left.
quests.sentence: She asked, 'What time does the train leave?'
quests.hint: In wh-questions, use statement word order. 'Does' disappears and tense shifts.
quests.explanation: In reported wh-questions, use statement order (no auxiliary 'does'). 'Leave' shifts to 'left'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: They asked, 'Can we stay here tonight?'
options: They asked if they could stay here tonight.
They asked if they could stay there that night.
They asked could they stay there that night.
quests.correctAnswer: They asked if they could stay there that night.
quests.sentence: They asked, 'Can we stay here tonight?'
quests.hint: 'Can' → 'could', 'here' → 'there', and 'tonight' → 'that night'.
quests.explanation: Multiple shifts: 'can' → 'could', 'here' → 'there', and 'tonight' → 'that night'. Use 'if' and statement word order.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She asked, 'Are you happy?'
options: She asked if I am happy.
She asked if I was happy.
She asked was I happy.
quests.correctAnswer: She asked if I was happy.
quests.sentence: She asked, 'Are you happy?'
quests.hint: Yes/No questions use 'if'. 'Are' shifts to 'was' and word order becomes subject + verb.
quests.explanation: Yes/No questions in reported speech use 'if', and the word order becomes subject-verb. 'Are' shifts to 'was'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The detective asked, 'Where were you last night?'
options: The detective asked where I was the night before.
The detective asked where I had been the night before.
The detective asked where was I the night before.
quests.correctAnswer: The detective asked where I had been the night before.
quests.sentence: The detective asked, 'Where were you last night?'
quests.hint: 'Were' shifts to 'had been' (past perfect), and 'last night' shifts to 'the night before'.
quests.explanation: Past simple 'were' shifts to past perfect 'had been'. 'Last night' becomes 'the night before'. Statement word order is used.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: He said, 'I wish I were rich.'
options: He said that he wished he were rich.
He said that he wished he was rich.
He said that he had wished he were rich.
quests.correctAnswer: He said that he wished he were rich.
quests.sentence: He said, 'I wish I were rich.'
quests.hint: 'Wish' shifts to 'wished'. The subjunctive 'were' remains 'were' in formal English.
quests.explanation: 'Wish' shifts to 'wished'. The subjunctive form 'were' is typically retained in reported speech after 'wish'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: They told us, 'We have already left.'
options: They told us that they had already left.
They told us that they have already left.
They told us that they already left.
quests.correctAnswer: They told us that they had already left.
quests.sentence: They told us, 'We have already left.'
quests.hint: Present perfect ('have left') shifts to past perfect ('had left').
quests.explanation: 'Have left' (present perfect) shifts to 'had left' (past perfect) in reported speech. 'Already' stays in position.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: He told me, 'Open the window, please.'
options: He told me to open the window.
He asked me to open the window.
He said to me open the window.
quests.correctAnswer: He asked me to open the window.
quests.sentence: He told me, 'Open the window, please.'
quests.hint: A polite request ('please') is best reported with 'asked + object + to + infinitive'.
quests.explanation: When 'please' is used, it signals a request rather than a command. 'Asked me to open' is the natural reported form.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She remarked, 'If I had seen the sign, I would have stopped.'
options: She remarked that if she had seen the sign, she would have stopped.
She remarked that if she saw the sign, she would have stopped.
She remarked that if she had seen the sign, she would stop.
quests.correctAnswer: She remarked that if she had seen the sign, she would have stopped.
quests.sentence: She remarked, 'If I had seen the sign, I would have stopped.'
quests.hint: The third conditional ('had seen / would have stopped') cannot shift back further.
quests.explanation: Third conditional structures ('had seen / would have stopped') are already in past perfect and conditional perfect - they do not shift further in reported speech.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: He stated, 'The project will be a success.'
options: He stated that the project would be a success.
He stated that the project will be a success.
He stated that the project was a success.
quests.correctAnswer: He stated that the project would be a success.
quests.sentence: He stated, 'The project will be a success.'
quests.hint: 'Will' shifts to 'would' in reported speech.
quests.explanation: 'Will be' shifts to 'would be' in reported speech. The subject stays as 'the project'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The officer ordered, 'Stand up immediately.'
options: The officer ordered us to stand up immediately.
The officer said that we stand up immediately.
The officer ordered that we stood up immediately.
quests.correctAnswer: The officer ordered us to stand up immediately.
quests.sentence: The officer ordered, 'Stand up immediately.'
quests.hint: Commands use 'ordered + object + to + infinitive'.
quests.explanation: When reporting orders, use 'ordered + object + to + infinitive'. 'Stand up' becomes 'to stand up'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The captain shouted, 'Abandon ship at once!'
options: The captain shouted that we abandon ship at once.
The captain ordered to abandon ship at once.
The captain ordered us to abandon ship immediately.
quests.correctAnswer: The captain ordered us to abandon ship immediately.
quests.sentence: The captain shouted, 'Abandon ship at once!'
quests.hint: Urgent commands use 'ordered + object + to + infinitive'. 'At once' can shift to 'immediately'.
quests.explanation: 'Shouted' signals urgency; the reported form uses 'ordered + us + to + infinitive'. 'At once' naturally becomes 'immediately' in formal reported speech.
